item.title: Rapid Reaction: Northwestern falls 20-17 in heartbreaker to Minnesota
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Nicco Marchiol (4) celebrates his touchdown against the Minnesota Golden Gophers during the second half at Huntington Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Northwestern loses in heartbreaking fashion as it falls to Minnesota 20-17. In a game that looked poised to go to overtime after the ‘Cats scored with just 27 seconds remaining in the game, Minnesota gave payback for last year’s Wrigley Field matchup by kicking a walk-off field goal to win the game. Nicco Marchiol had a solid day and performed well in the eye test, but there were a plethora of incompletions that could have altered the result of the game. He completed 13-of-23 passing attempts for 169 yards and a touchdown. For the first time in quite a while, Northwestern found some room in the run game with running back Caleb Komolafe rushing 19 times for 109 yards. Griffin Wilde also had a solid game, catching five passes for 77 yards and a touchdown. Luke Dehnicke showed his emerging talent as a tight end, catching three passes for 66 yards. This game marks the first four-game losing streak in the David Braun era at Northwestern. The Gophers kicked it away for a touchback to open the penultimate regular-season game. The ‘Cats’ offense started things off with runs to Komolafe and Drew Wagner, picking up the first down to move the chains. Komolafe then broke off a 14-yard run to keep things going, but Minnesota’s defense forced an incompletion and short run to bring up third down. Another Marchiol incompletion to Wilde brought out Northwestern’s punt unit, and the Gophers’ first possession started at their own 20. Minnesota QB Drake Lindsey started out in the air with completions to his tight end Roman Voss and running back Darius Taylor to bring up a third-and-4. The ‘Cats stood strong, and Jamaal Johnson got home for a sack to force the punt. The three-and-out gave NU the ball right back at the 43-yard line. On offense, a second-down jet sweep to Drew Wagner squeaked the ‘Cats past the first-down marker, but then Marchiol and Wilde failed to connect yet again to put NU behind schedule. A fake handoff led to Marchiol being drilled behind the line of scrimmage, setting up a third-and-15 where Sawchuk’s run barely got back to the initial line of scrimmage. Minnesota’s game plan stayed the same on its second drive, opening with a short pass to Jalen Smith and a short run by Darius Taylor to pick up a first down. After two short gains, Northwestern surged into the backfield on third-and-short, but Minnesota’s TJ Thomas’ second effort kept the drive alive. Thomas then picked up 18 yards on a short completion as the Gopher offense found a rhythm and moved to the Northwestern 42. However, a holding call a couple of plays later led to Minnesota stalling out and setting up a 48-yard field goal try. The Gophers’ kicker pulled the ball left, and the game remained scoreless.

item.title: Ravens’ 2026 season has come to a crashing halt
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Trainers attend to Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens kneels after getting hurt on the first play of the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images It took just one play. As optimistically as it began, the 2026 Ravens season is all but finished. On the first day of November, on his first snap back from a high-ankle sprain, Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb when his throwing hand struck the wrist of Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau. Jackson knew something was wrong immediately, sprinting straight to the sideline and then to the locker room. The two-time MVP has since had surgery on his thumb with a late-season return technically in play – if it even matters. At this point, Jackson is the Baltimore Ravens, and his contract reflects that. Many want to bash the supporting cast, the coaches and the front office, but it just isn’t realistic for a team paying a star quarterback that much to also have stars at every other position. What did the Chiefs look like without Patrick Mahomes last year? What did the Bengals look like without Joe Burrow? What would the Bills look like without Josh Allen? On top of losing Jackson, the Ravens have suffered a rash of injuries elsewhere, primarily on the offensive line. A position group that typically thrives on continuity is operating with a new offensive coordinator, a new offensive line coach, and a rotating door of new starters. This year, the unit has had five different centers and four different right guards. Has the offensive line been good enough? No. But we never got to see the vision. Heck, we never even got to see Jackson and Zay Flowers play a full game together. The full extent of the Ravens’ woes came to a head five days after the Jacksonville Jaguars. With undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano making his first start, the Ravens were once again trounced at home, this time in a downpour. We all expected the offense to struggle, and predictably, it did. But once again, the defense let the dam break. Is that partly a product of the offense’s struggles? Probably. Still, it looked more like a group of unmotivated, aging players struggling to adjust to a new defensive system. Marlon Humphrey and Malaki Starks were both burned for big plays, and the middle of the field — an area that has plagued this defense for years — was wide open all night for Trevor Lawrence. And yet, Monday night’s loss to the Chargers might have been worse. Jacoby Brissett performed admirable in his Ravens debut, but an anemic running game and a defense that once again could not tackle gifted a winless team their first victory. Unfortunately, the near future doesn’t look much brighter, largely because of some questionable decisions by the front office. item.title: Browns Get Credit for Contract Move on $13 Million Newcomer
item.description: Quincy Williams #5 of the Cleveland Browns Getty Most of the offseason for the Cleveland Browns was focused first on the overhaul of the offensive line in March, followed by another big NFL draft haul in April, one which was widely predicted to be successful (and has probably even exceeded those expectations). But tucked in among those move was an underrated one: the Browns brought in a favorite of new defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg by signing former Jets linebacker Quincy Williams, whose style of play on the field is as dynamic as his mouth can be during interviews. Rutenberg was Williams’ position coach with the Jets, and Williams was an All-Pro in 2023 under Rutenberg’s watch. After signing a two-year, $13 million contract ($17 million with incentives), Williams said, “Not to be cocky, but the first thing (Retunberg) did was come and get me.” The move has worked. The Browns lost productive linebacker Devin Bush after last season, and needed a new running mate for star Carson Schwesinger. So far, Williams has fit the bill. He is rated the No. 7 linebacker in the league at Pro Football Focus, out of 82 in total. Quincy Williams a Success for the Browns At ESPN, the Browns’ signing of Williams–which has been largely overlooked–got some praise in an article by Aaron Schatz. Browns LB Quincy Williams: “They be barking. We be biting.” pic.twitter.com/kTXVyxOYWG — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) October 2, 2026 He writes : “Quincy Williams had only 12 starts for the Jets last season and turned 30 in August, so it was reasonable to assume that he was at the tail end of his career. The Browns brought him in on a reasonable contract and stuck him next to Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger , and Williams has been an outstanding playmaker in that role. … “Williams is known for speed and has been excellent in pass coverage, with four passes defensed and 15 pass tackles, which prevented a successful yardage gain despite a reception. Opposing running backs have fewer than 20 receiving yards per game against the Browns.” Two of Williams’ biggest incentives are still possible, but they are longshots –$500,000 for four sacks, and $500,000 for three interceptions. That would double if the Browns make the playoffs, which they are in good position to do. item.title: Dixon becomes tenth Illini to reach 1,000 single-season receving yards
item.description: Collin Dixon leads the nation in TD receptions after three games. | TCR / David Pollak CHAMPAIGN, Ill — As of late, it seems as though everything Colin Dixon touches turns to gold. The senior wideout has yet again made history this season as he is now the tenth Illini to ever record a 1,000+ receving yards in a single season. He is the first Illini since Isiash Willams in 2023 to achieve such a milestone. Another milestone achieved. Collin Dixon becomes the 10th player in program history to rack up 1,000 receiving yards in a season. pic.twitter.com/iUVcvaoqNB — Illinois Football (@IlliniFootball) November 21, 2026 The last home game prior to this, Colin Dixon made history once again as a two-yard pass was touchdown number 11 for the recevier, setting a new program touchdown record which was once held by former Illini turned Denver Bronco, Pat Bryant. The catch that put Dixon into the four digit club was a flea-flicker from QB Katin Houser, who was a game-time decision heading into Illinois final home outing of the season against the Iowa Hawkeyes. With another half of football, followed by the battle for the land of Lincoln trophy out in Evanston against the Northwestern Wildcats, Dixon has plently of time to keeping adding to this record breaking season.

item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) drives for a shot against Milwaukee Bucks center Myles Turner (3) during the second quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Joel Embiid’s 26-point, 17-rebound effort was enough to push the Sixers past Tyler Herro’s 50-point night, with Philadelphia escaping 132-129 after Herro’s last-second three was ruled out. LeBron James added 21-6-6 to guide the 76ers to the win. Here’s what I saw. Just good enough to win This was a classic edition of a 1 pm game against a nonsense team for the Sixers. The first 24 minutes featured pretty miserable defense, no attention to detail on the glass, and some funky lineups for Philadelphia. But they had beautiful passing in half-court offense and ran the floor well, so they emerged with a one-point lead at halftime while exerting close to minimal effort. This was not the usual Embiid sautee of Myles Turner, who did a good job of bothering his shots and minimizing foul trouble in the first half. But Embiid’s shot was the only thing missing from an otherwise complete half, as he spent most of it playmaking out of the high post as the Bucks let cutters waltz down the middle of the lane. item.title: Davies explains Birmingham star’s absence against Stoke – and reacts to defeat
item.description: Davies explains Birmingham star’s absence against Stoke – and reacts to defeat Birmingham City boss Chris Davies admits his side deserved to lose their against Stoke City. George Hirst scored the only goal shortly after half-time to knock Blues off the top of the Championship, despite Birmingham playing against ten men for the final half an hour after Luca Bombino was sent off. “We needed to do more,” Davies said on his side’s performance after the red card. “I expected us to do more than we did with that amount of time. Creativity is a good word to highlight. “Sometimes it’s about getting crosses in, causing that little bit of chaos, seeing if we can get a second ball, and not trying to score the perfect goal basically. “Then you go to the quality of the crossing, arriving in the right positions, and it was all just off the level it needed to be. “You always have to give credit when the opposition holds on and does it doggedly like Stoke did. Fair play to them for that but we expect more from ourselves.” Davies also provided an update on Jhon Solis, who missed the game after picking up a knock while on international duty. “Jhon picked up a knock on international duty that we thought he would run off,” he said. “But he wasn’t able to do that. “My understanding is that it’s not a long-term thing but it was investigated more today so we should know tomorrow.” Asked whether Solis could be available on Wednesday, Davies added: “I think there is a chance but I don’t know how big that chance is right now based on what I was told yesterday.”

item.title: Fans with Saturday tickets to RSM Classic are out of luck, no gallery for final round Monday
item.description: Heavy rain led to poor course conditions at Sea Island Resort's Seaside Course in St. Simon's Island, Georgia, forcing the PGA Tour to postpone Saturday's third round of the 2026 RSM Classic to Sunday and push the final round back to Monday. So what about fans who had tickets to see Saturday's action in-person? Tough luck. The RSM Classic put out a statement on social media Saturday afternoon noting that only fans with tickets for Sunday would be allowed in the gates for the third round. "Only Sunday tickets will be accepted tomorrow," the tournament wrote in an Instagram post . "Due to our refund and exchange policy, we will not honor Saturday tickets tomorrow." The tournament also said no spectators will be in attendance for Monday's final round, meaning the last 18 holes of the PGA Tour's 2026 season will be played without a gallery. "Grounds will be closed to all patrons on Monday," the post's caption read. "Golf Channel will televise the event so watch there." There's a three-way tie atop the leaderboard after 36 holes between Michael Thorbjornsen, Marco Penge and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen, and there are another 13 players within two shots of the lead. It's also crunch time for several players who are fighting to get inside the top 100 in the FedEx Cup standings, the threshold required to keep a PGA Tour card for the 2027 season. item.title: Grading Purdue football: Questionable QB decision and Fs all-around in blowout loss to Wisconsin
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − Purdue football 's nose dive continues. The Boilermakers had the ball just 49 seconds before they trailed 14-0. Wisconsin (7-4) had the opening it needed on its way to a 42-10 victory . The Badgers sent Purdue (3-8) fans exiting the season's final home game with a fifth straight loss, and now with 19 consecutive losses in the series. A questionable starting quarterback decision backfired and Purdue's wet paper bag defense again provided a big day for a struggling offense. In a season marred by failures, you can imagine how the report card looks from Purdue's loss to Wisconsin at Ross-Ade Stadium. OFFENSE GRADE: F The offensive line was supposed to be an upgrade this year, but it's becoming hard to find evidence supporting that claim. Not a lot of analysis needs to go into this grade. Statistics are all you need. Purdue averaged 3.6 yards per play and totaled 199 yards. DEFENSE GRADE: F By halftime, the Badgers already had accumulated 52 more rushing yards (185) than their season average (133). Purdue's defense is beyond repair. Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph didn't start the last two games but returned behind center after Ryan Hopkins was injured late in a Nov. 14 game against Maryland. Joseph then became the latest QB to torch the Big Ten's worst defense. The Badgers totaled 508 yards, 381 of those on the ground. Wisconsin was 13-for-17 on converting third and fourth downs. SPECIAL TEAMS GRADE: B Jacobo Echeverria Lozano attempted, and made, a career-long 53-yard field goal in the second quarter. It pads his case for the Lou Groza Award, which is bolstered because Purdue's offense is good, but not good enough to get into the end zone in a lot of cases. Still, the freshman has taken advantage. Dylan Drennan also has been a weapon, though Purdue doesn't have a competent enough defense to fully benefit from Drennan's leg. The risk returning kickoffs has not paid off. Best bet for Purdue is to take the touchback, or fair catch if the kickoff doesn't reach the end zone. COACHING GRADE: F You can't give me a valid reason why quarterback Evans Chuba started this game over Ryan Browne. No package or perceived advantage makes sense. It's even more indefensible after seeing the results of that decision. Chuba threw two incompletions during a three-and-out. Browne led Purdue on consecutive scoring drives after entering. Purdue had a second week to tinker with the defense since Kevin Kane's firing , and somehow looked better on the road against a ranked Iowa team with little time to adapt to the staff change. Waiting until you're down 18 points to uncover the trick play portion of the playbook seems like off timing. GAME MVP If Ryan Hopkins is healthy, Colton Joseph probably doesn't even start this game. Instead, Joseph's return as the Badgers starting quarterback. He rushed for 187 yards and 2 touchdowns, passed for 114 yards and also hauled in a 13-yard touchdown reception. item.title: FAMU football QB Armond Parker returns as starter vs Bethune-Cookman
item.description: Armond Parker is back in the fold as Florida A&M 's starting quarterback for the Saturday's season finale at the Florida Classic. The true freshman took the field to lead the Rattlers offense on the opening drive against rivals Bethune-Cookman at Orlando’s Camping World Stadium. Parker missed last week’s game against Mississippi Valley State, which the Rattlers won 16-13 . Head coach Quinn Fordham Gray Sr. held the quarterback out because he was “beat up” from the grind of the season . James Hayes started instead and went 14-for-27 for 144 passing yards, a touchdown, and threw two interceptions in his second career start. Gray told local media earlier this week that Parker was still in the “evaluation process” and expected him to “be okay.” Parker practiced this week. Parker has been the starter since midseason, after quarterback injuries piled up on the Rattlers. The Bethune-Cookman Wildcats matchup is his seventh start, fresh out of Locust Grove High School. He enters Week 12 as the fifth-leading passer in the Southwestern Athletic Conference with 1790 yards. Parker also adds 14 passing touchdowns, rushed for three, and has thrown 11 interceptions. item.title: MLS star Thomas Muller explains how promotion and relegation changes league dynamic
item.description: MLS star Thomas Muller explains how promotion and relegation changes league dynamic originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Now 37 years old, Thomas Muller has greatly enjoyed his time in Major League Soccer. After leaving Bayern Munich in the summer of 2025 following a glittering 17-year career with the Bavarian giants, Muller joined the Vancouver Whitecaps and has brought his winning mentality along. Muller reached the MLS Cup final in his first half-season, losing to Lionel Messi and Inter Miami at the final hurdle. This season, Vancouver won the Western Conference regular season title, and are set to be the No. 1 seed on their side of the bracket in the playoffs. Always his enlightening, outspoken self, Muller took the time to explain how MLS is different without promotion and relegation, from a player's perspective. He believes there are real, on-field consequences to having a closed pyramid, ones which players can notice by the style of play across the league. MORE: Explaining the Jamal Musiala contract dispute which has Bayern Munich receiving criticism Thomas Muller explains how MLS is different without relegation Thomas Muller was asked how he feels Major League Soccer handles being a closed, single-entity league without promotion and relegation. The 37-year-old stopped short of criticizing the league for not having promotion and relegation, but he did explain the differences between having open movement throughout the pyramid and having a closed system without the threat of relegation at the bottom of the table. As Muller explains, there is a pressure for those under relegation threat that changes the way some teams play. Without that threat, as there is in MLS, teams play more openly — more risky, as Muller insinuates — which can increase the range of possible performances. It can cause players to make excellent plays, but also commit grave errors you wouldn't see in a less-risky playing style at a team battling relegation. "There is no relegation," Muller explained at the end of the 2026 regular season. "There is no big pressure. There is 'oh yea, we do a rebuild.' Nobody's happy to lose, but it's totally different when you fight for getting relegated. Maybe you lose, but for the whole year, the whole club, you lose people working at the club and the budget changes. It's totally different for fans, the pressure. The players maybe have no contract for next year when you go down. "So the playing style changes. When you play a bottom-of-the-league team in Europe, they fight for their lives. That’s not just from an individual perspective, though Simmons has been great in that regard, posting three tackles for loss, two sacks, and two passes defended in his two weeks with the Bears. The unit as a whole has benefited from the increased double teams the All-Pro tackle has faced, allowing just 4.5 yards per play when he’s been on the field and ranking in the top 10 in EPA/play and success rate allowed since Simmons got here. But there’s one aspect in which, while improved, the Bears have remained somewhat middling at: defending the run. That’s why NFL.com ‘s Brooke Cersosimo forecasts New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne might be a problem for Chicago on Sunday. “Etienne returned to action last week after missing five games with a hamstring injury and looked rusty — to say the least — rushing for 14 yards on eight carries. He turns things around in dramatic fashion against the Bears on Sunday with his first 100-yard rushing performance and touchdown of the season,” Cersosimo wrote for her bold prediction for this week in NFL action. That’s definitely a choice. When healthy, Etienne is one of the better dual-threat backs in the league. In fact, no one in New Orleans running backs room has done much worth writing home about: through nine games, quarterback Tyler Shough leads the team with 187 rushing yards. That’s ugly. The Saints have a true running-by-committee squad, ravaged by a combination of injuries and ineffectiveness. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.) item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
